card: Updates sock_tests/send_and_receive to read socket data across multiple Recv calls instead of expecting the full 4-byte payload in one call. This fixes an assumption in test code where chunked or partial network reads could lead to intermittent test failure. The vulnerability was verified using an artificial chunking patch in test run #36751.
evidence: Author notes the failure can be triggered with a forced-chunking reproducer: 'This was found -- and can be reproduced -- by using a reproducer patch, that forces all socket sends to use smaller chunking. For the run with the reproducer see #36751.'
Author clarifies scope in the description: 'The issue is test-code only, the non-test code is correct.'
problem: The unit test assumes that a 4-byte socket read completes in a single Recv call. While partial reads are improbable in standard CI runs on loopback, socket semantics do not guarantee full delivery in one call, risking intermittent test failures under chunked delivery.

risk.why: A flaw in the test loop could cause test timeouts or false test failures in sock_tests.

scope_notes: Very small change (+8/-1) isolated to a single unit test.
summary: Updates the sock_tests/send_and_receive unit test to read from the socket in a loop until all expected bytes arrive. This avoids assuming the entire payload will be returned in a single Recv call.
